obligation: Local law enforcement and county emergency management
citation: FERC Security Program Rev. 3A, sec. 4.2 and 7.4.1 (Internal Emergency Response sub-element)
trigger: Serious security incident, including any unauthorized operation of gates or units
deadline: Immediately, in parallel with safe-state actions
notify: County sheriff (911); county emergency management for the DEV-05 inundation zone
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all Hydro projects
notifying_entity: Hydro (HOC shift supervisor or Director, Hydro Security)

trigger: Impending or actual sudden release of water (project emergency, 18 CFR 12.3(b)(9))
deadline: Immediately, per the EAP notification flowchart
notify: Downstream residents (sirens); county emergency management; agencies listed in the EAP
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the event becomes a project emergency
notifying_entity: Hydro (Chief Dam Safety Engineer; HOC shift supervisor may activate)

obligation: Condition affecting safety of project works: initial report
trigger: Gate misoperation, unusual instrumentation readings, or a security incident (physical and/or cyber)
deadline: As soon as practicable after discovery, preferably within 72 hours, without unduly interfering with emergency action
notify: FERC Regional Engineer by email or telephone
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Hydro is the licensee

obligation: Condition affecting safety of project works: written report
trigger: After the initial report
deadline: Within the time the Regional Engineer specifies; verified under 12.13
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Deaths, serious injuries, or rescues at the project
trigger: Any death, serious injury, or rescue at the project works or involving project operation, including changes in flows caused by project gates
deadline: Initial report promptly after discovery; written report for project-related events
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if any occur (for example, boaters caught by the release below DEV-05)

obligation: Security incident report to the FERC Regional Office
citation: FERC Security Program Rev. 3A, sec. 3.2 (bullet 11) and 4.2
trigger: Security incident or suspicious activity at a project, unless law enforcement restricts reporting
deadline: As soon as practical (usually within one working day)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - can be combined with the 12.10 initial report

obligation: Temporary closure of recreation facilities for security
trigger: Recreation areas closed for security for 30 days or less
deadline: As soon as practical (usually within one working day); closures over 30 days need prior coordination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if areas below DEV-05 are closed

obligation: Other dam owners in the drainage basin
trigger: Security situation that could affect other dam owners (flows into downstream reservoirs)
deadline: As quickly as possible
notify: Operators of the 2 downstream projects on the river (basin coordination agreement)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Suspicious activity report to the HSIN Dams portal
citation: FERC Security Program Rev. 3A, sec. 4.2; Appendix B
trigger: Suspicious activity or security incident
deadline: No deadline stated; report promptly
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary but highly recommended

obligation: Low impact Reportable Cyber Security Incident notification
trigger: Determination that a Cyber Security Incident at a low impact BES plant is a Reportable Cyber Security Incident (for example, the DEV-05 Unit 2 governor setpoint change)
deadline: No deadline in the standard; Hydro's plan sets 1 hour after determination, to match the medium impact clock
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - DEV-05 is a low impact BES plant

trigger: Determination that a Cyber Security Incident compromised or disrupted a HOC BES Cyber System, its ESP, or its EACMS
deadline: Within 1 hour after the determination; attributes: functional impact, attack vector, level of intrusion
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the HOC systems were compromised or disrupted

trigger: Determination, using the plan's Part 1.2.1 criteria, that the incident was an attempt to compromise a HOC BES Cyber System or EACMS (for example, the blocked connections from DEV-05 toward the HOC ESP)
deadline: By the end of the next calendar day after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the criteria are met

trigger: New or changed attribute information
deadline: Within 7 calendar days of determining the new or changed information
applies_at_this_tier: Yes after any initial notification

trigger: For a GO or GOP: damage or destruction of its Facility from actual or suspected intentional human action, or a physical threat or suspicious device or activity at its Facility
deadline: By the later of 24 hours after recognizing the event threshold or the end of the next business day (4 p.m. local time)
notify: Entities in the EOP-004 Operating Plan (ERO via systemawareness@nerc.net; SERC; law enforcement)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a threshold is met (for example, hoist or unit damage, or an unauthorized device found at the plant)

obligation: Form DOE-417 Electric Emergency Incident and Disturbance Report
trigger: Cyber event criteria on the form (for example, a cyber event that interrupts electrical system operations, or one that could affect reliability), or an attempted cyber compromise
deadline: Emergency Alert criteria within 1 hour; Normal Report criteria within 6 hours; attempted cyber compromise by the end of the next calendar day after determination; final report within 72 hours
notify: DOE Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the Balancing Authority does not file for the event (coordinate with the BA)
notifying_entity: Hydro (NERC Compliance Director) or the Balancing Authority
clock_starts: The incident (or the determination, for attempts)

obligation: Balancing Authority and Transmission Operator operational notice
trigger: Change in unit availability or an event affecting the ICCP link
deadline: Immediately by phone from the HOC
notify: The Balancing Authority and Transmission Operator control center for DEV-05
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - operational

citation: FERC Security Program Rev. 3A, sec. 9.4 (coordination with authorities such as the FBI); CISA voluntary reporting
trigger: Suspected intrusion into control systems
deadline: As soon as possible; no regulatory deadline
notify: FBI field office (or IC3) and CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary; strongly advised. Also a mitigating factor for OFAC

trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident affecting a covered contractor information system or covered defense information (the compromised commissioning laptop held USACE CUI drawings synced from another project)
deadline: Rapidly report: within 72 hours of discovery, using a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Constructors holds 11 USACE contracts with the clause

trigger: Malicious software discovered and isolated in connection with a reported incident
deadline: With the report, as DC3 or the contracting officer instructs
notify: DoD Cyber Crime Center (DC3); not the contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if malware is isolated

trigger: Cyber incident reported under (c)
deadline: Preserve images of affected systems and monitoring data for at least 90 days from the report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Covered equipment found in use (for example, if the cellular router or a jobsite camera is a covered brand)
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further information within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Only if covered equipment is identified
notifying_entity: Constructors or Engineering (Federal Programs Compliance Director)

trigger: A Kaspersky covered article found during the investigation
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Only where the clause is included and an article is identified
notifying_entity: Constructors or Engineering (Federal Programs Compliance Director)

trigger: A covered article subject to a FASCSA order found during the investigation
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Only where the clause is included and an article is identified
notifying_entity: Constructors or Engineering (Federal Programs Compliance Director)

trigger: Client drawings or facility security details were on the compromised laptop
deadline: Per each contract (most require prompt notice; 3 require 72 hours)
notify: Owners of the other projects whose files were on the laptop
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

citation: DSMS master agreement, security schedule sec. 4 (contract)
trigger: Security incident affecting a client's DSMS data (for example, if the attacker used the two-way DEV-05 replication to reach the DSMS)
deadline: Within 48 hours of confirmation
notify: Each affected DSMS client's security contact
applies_at_this_tier: Only if DSMS client data is affected; Engineering must check the DEV-05 replication path

trigger: Client CEII exposed
deadline: Per NDA terms (prompt notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if client CEII was exposed

trigger: The disclosure committee determines the incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay possible only on a U.S. Attorney General finding)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the group is an SEC registrant

trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents (crew badging list: names and driver's license numbers)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (15-day extension only for good cause, for this notice only)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Florida residents are on the list

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if 500 or more Floridians

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Only if more than 1,000 individuals

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents of other states (crew members from Tennessee, Georgia, and Alabama)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Affected residents; state regulators where required
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any extortion demand and a payment under consideration
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier hotline before hiring vendors)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; the group would likely be covered if finalized as proposed
